title: Which of these equal ninety one minus thirty five minus twelve?
description: Three expressions are compared with ninety one minus thirty five minus twelve by reading their terms with signs. Opening a bracket after a minus flips every sign inside. Keeko doubts that the second bracket keeps its signs.
teaching_notes: One idea: compare expressions by their terms with signs, and remember that a minus in front of a bracket flips every sign inside. Watch for students who open a bracket after a minus without changing the signs.

video_script.why: A learner decides which expressions are equal by reading terms with signs after opening each bracket.
video_script.substitution: Replace ninety one, thirty five and twelve with any three numbers and compare in the same way.
video_script.anchor: ninety one minus thirty five minus twelve, and three expressions to compare with it
video_script.wrong_answer: the second bracket keeps its signs when it opens
video_script.wrong_move: opens 91 − (35 − 12) without flipping the signs inside the bracket, so the − 12 stays − 12
video_script.payoff_line: The first and third are equal to it, and the second is not.

final_answer.spoken: the first and third are equal to it, and the second is not

maths_rules: −35 + 91 − 12 has the terms −35, 91 and −12, in a new order
the slip: the − 12 inside the bracket stays − 12 instead of flipping to + 12
video_script.design: The target expression sits at the top as three signed terms. Each of the three other expressions is opened and its signed terms are matched against the target, term by term.

narration: <bookmark mark='s21'/>Step two, open the first bracket.
The minus in front changes the sign of each term inside.
<bookmark mark='s22'/>Plus thirty five becomes minus thirty five, and plus twelve becomes minus twelve.
<bookmark mark='s23'/>We get ninety one minus thirty five minus twelve, the same terms as the target. These are equal.

The terms are minus thirty five, ninety one and minus twelve.
<bookmark mark='s32'/>These are the same terms in a new order, and order does not change a sum. These are equal.

narration: <bookmark mark='s41'/>Step four, open the second bracket.
The minus in front changes the sign of each term inside.
<bookmark mark='s42'/>Plus thirty five becomes minus thirty five, and minus twelve becomes plus twelve.
<bookmark mark='s43'/>We get ninety one minus thirty five plus twelve. The target has minus twelve, so these are not equal.
